content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Regem regum Dóminum veníte adorémus: * Quia ipse est coróna Sanctórum ómnium.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship the Lord, the King of kings, * for He is Himself the Crown of all the Saints.

segments.t: Ant.
Regem regum Dóminum veníte adorémus: * Quia ipse est coróna Sanctórum ómnium.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Quia ipse est coróna Sanctórum ómnium.
content.english: Ant. for He is Himself the Crown of all the Saints.

segments.t: Ant.
Quia ipse est coróna Sanctórum ómnium.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

segments.t: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius

content.latin: Ant. Regem regum Dóminum veníte adorémus: * Quia ipse est coróna Sanctórum ómnium.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship the Lord, the King of kings, * for He is Himself the Crown of all the Saints.

segments.t: Ant.
Regem regum Dóminum veníte adorémus: * Quia ipse est coróna Sanctórum ómnium.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Quia ipse est coróna Sanctórum ómnium.
content.english: Ant. for He is Himself the Crown of all the Saints.

segments.t: Ant.
Quia ipse est coróna Sanctórum ómnium.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Placáre, Christe, sérvulis,
content.english: O Christ, thy guilty people spare!

content.latin: Quibus Patris cleméntiam
content.english: Lo, kneeling at thy gracious throne,

content.latin: Tuæ ad tribúnal grátiæ
content.english: thy Virgin-Mother pours her prayer,

content.latin: Patróna Virgo póstulat.
content.english: Imploring pardon for her own.

content.latin: Et vos beáta, per novem
content.english: Ye angels, happy evermore!

content.latin: Distíncta gyros ágmina,
content.english: Who in your circles nine ascend,

content.latin: Antíqua cum præséntibus,
content.english: As ye have guarded us before,

content.latin: Futúra damna péllite.
content.english: So still from harm our steps defend.

content.latin: Apóstoli cum Vátibus,
content.english: Ye prophets and Apostles high!

content.latin: Apud sevérum Iúdicem,
content.english: Behold our penitential tears;

content.latin: Veris reórum flétibus
content.english: And plead for us when death is nigh,

content.latin: Expóscite indulgéntiam.
content.english: our all-searching judge appears.

content.latin: Vos, purpuráti mártyres,
content.english: Ye martyrs all! a purple band,

content.latin: Vos candidáti prǽmio
content.english: And confessors, a white-robed train;

content.latin: Confessiónis, éxsules
content.english: Oh, call us to our native land,

content.latin: Vocáte nos in pátriam.
content.english: From this our exile, back again.

content.latin: Choréa casta vírginum,
content.english: And ye, O choirs of virgins chaste!

content.latin: Et quos erémus íncolas
content.english: Receive us to your seats on high;

content.latin: Transmísit astris, cǽlitum
content.english: With hermits whom the desert waste

content.latin: Locáte nos in sédibus.
content.english: Sent up of old into the sky.

content.latin: Auférte gentem pérfidam
content.english: Drive from the flock, O Spirit blest!

content.latin: Credéntium de fínibus,
content.english: The false and faithless race away;

content.latin: Ut unus omnes únicum
content.english: That all within one fold may rest,

content.latin: Ovíle nos Pastor regat.
content.english: Secure beneath one shepherd's sway.

content.latin: Deo Patri sit glória,
content.english: To God the Father glory be,

content.latin: Natóque Patris único,
content.english: And to his sole-begotten Son;

content.latin: Sancto simul Paráclito,
content.english: And glory, Holy Ghost, to thee,

content.latin: In sempitérna sǽcula.
content.english: While everlasting ages run.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.english: Ant. The Lord knoweth the way of the righteous, * who in His Law do meditate day and night.

content.latin: Psalmus 1 [1]
content.english: Psalm 1 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 1

content.latin: 1:1 Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:
content.english: 1:1 Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, * nor sat in the chair of pestilence.

segments.t: Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:

content.latin: 1:2 Sed in lege Dómini volúntas eius, * et in lege eius meditábitur die ac nocte.
content.english: 1:2 But his will is in the law of the Lord, * and on his law he shall meditate day and night.

segments.t: Sed in lege Dómini volúntas eius, * et in lege eius meditábitur die ac nocte.

content.latin: 1:3 Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:
content.english: 1:3 And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, * which shall bring forth its fruit, in due season.

segments.t: Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:

content.latin: 1:3 Et fólium eius non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.
content.english: 1:3 And his leaf shall not fall off: * and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.

segments.t: Et fólium eius non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.

content.latin: 1:4 Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.
content.english: 1:4 Not so the wicked, not so: * but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth.

segments.t: Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.

content.latin: 1:5 Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in iudício: * neque peccatóres in concílio iustórum.
content.english: 1:5 Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment: * nor sinners in the council of the just.

segments.t: Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in iudício: * neque peccatóres in concílio iustórum.

content.latin: 1:6 Quóniam novit Dóminus viam iustórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.
content.english: 1:6 For the Lord knoweth the way of the just: * and the way of the wicked shall perish.

segments.t: Quóniam novit Dóminus viam iustórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Ant. Mirificávit * Dóminus Sanctos suos, et exaudívit eos clamántes ad se.
content.english: Ant. The Lord hath set apart for Himself them that are holy, * and when they called, He hath heard them.

segments.t: Ant.
Mirificávit * Dóminus Sanctos suos, et exaudívit eos clamántes ad se.

content.latin: Psalmus 4 [2]
content.english: Psalm 4 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 4

content.latin: 4:2 Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus iustítiæ meæ: * in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.
content.english: 4:2 When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: * when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me.

segments.t: Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus iustítiæ meæ: * in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.

content.latin: 4:2 Miserére mei, * et exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: 4:2 Have mercy on me: * and hear my prayer.

segments.t: Miserére mei, * et exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: 4:3 Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?
content.english: 4:3 O ye sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart? * Why do you love vanity, and seek after lying?

segments.t: Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?

content.latin: 4:4 Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.
content.english: 4:4 Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: * the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him.

segments.t: Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.

content.latin: 4:5 Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.
content.english: 4:5 Be ye angry, and sin not: * the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds.

segments.t: Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.

content.latin: 4:6 Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?
content.english: 4:6 Offer up the sacrifice of justice, and trust in the Lord: * many say, Who sheweth us good things?

segments.t: Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?

content.latin: 4:7 Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
content.english: 4:7 The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: * thou hast given gladness in my heart.

segments.t: Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.

content.latin: 4:8 A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.
content.english: 4:8 By the fruit of their corn, their wine, and oil, * they are multiplied.

segments.t: A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.

content.latin: 4:9 In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;
content.english: 4:9 In peace in the selfsame * I will sleep, and I will rest:

segments.t: In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;

content.latin: 4:10 Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.
content.english: 4:10 For thou, O Lord, singularly * hast settled me in hope.

segments.t: Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Ant.
Mirificávit Dóminus Sanctos suos, et exaudívit eos clamántes ad se.

content.latin: Ant. Admirábile est * nomen tuum, Dómine: quia glória et honóre coronásti Sanctos tuos, et constituísti eos super ópera mánuum tuárum.
content.english: Ant. How excellent is thy Name, O Lord, Who hast crowned thy Saints with glory and honour, * and madest them to have dominion over the works of thy hands.

segments.t: Ant.
Admirábile est * nomen tuum, Dómine: quia glória et honóre coronásti Sanctos tuos, et constituísti eos super ópera mánuum tuárum.

content.latin: Psalmus 8 [3]
content.english: Psalm 8 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 8

content.latin: 8:2 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
content.english: 8:2 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!

segments.t: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!

content.latin: 8:2 Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.
content.english: 8:2 For thy magnificence is elevated * above the heavens.

segments.t: Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.

content.latin: 8:3 Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.
content.english: 8:3 Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise, because of thy enemies, * that thou mayst destroy the enemy and the avenger.

segments.t: Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.

content.latin: 8:4 Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.
content.english: 8:4 For I will behold thy heavens, the works of thy fingers: * the moon and the stars which thou hast founded.

segments.t: Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.

content.latin: 8:5 Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?
content.english: 8:5 What is man that thou art mindful of him? * or the son of man that thou visitest him?

segments.t: Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?

content.latin: 8:6 Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum: * et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
content.english: 8:6 Thou hast made him a little less than the angels, thou hast crowned him with glory and honour: * and hast set him over the works of thy hands.

segments.t: Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum: * et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.

content.latin: 8:8 Ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.
content.english: 8:8 Thou hast subjected all things under his feet, * all sheep and oxen: moreover the beasts also of the fields.

segments.t: Ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.

content.latin: 8:9 Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.
content.english: 8:9 The birds of the air, and the fishes of the sea, * that pass through the paths of the sea.

segments.t: Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.

content.latin: 8:10 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
content.english: 8:10 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in all the earth!

segments.t: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!

content.english: Ant. How excellent is thy Name, O Lord, Who hast crowned thy Saints with glory and honour, and madest them to have dominion over the works of thy hands.

segments.t: Ant.
Admirábile est nomen tuum, Dómine: quia glória et honóre coronásti Sanctos tuos, et constituísti eos super ópera mánuum tuárum.

content.latin: ℣. Lætámini in Dómino, et exsultáte iusti.
content.english: ℣. Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye just,

segments.t: Lætámini in Dómino, et exsultáte iusti.

content.latin: ℟. Et gloriámini omnes recti corde.
content.english: ℟. And glory, all ye right of heart.

segments.t: Et gloriámini omnes recti corde.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
content.english: Benediction. May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: De libro Apocalýpsis beáti Ioánnis Apóstoli
content.english: Lesson from the Apocalypse of St. John

content.latin: 2 Et ecce sedes pósita erat in cælo, et supra sedem sedens.
content.english: 2 And behold there was a throne set in heaven, and upon the throne one sitting.

segments.t: Et ecce sedes pósita erat in cælo, et supra sedem sedens.

content.latin: 3 Et qui sedébat símilis erat aspéctui lápidis iáspidis, et sárdinis: et iris erat in circúitu sedis símilis visióni smarágdinæ.
content.english: 3 And he that sat, was to the sight like the jasper and the sardine stone; and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald.

segments.t: Et qui sedébat símilis erat aspéctui lápidis iáspidis, et sárdinis: et iris erat in circúitu sedis símilis visióni smarágdinæ.

content.latin: 4 Et in circúitu sedis sedília vigínti quátuor: et super thronos vigínti quátuor senióres sedéntes, circumamícti vestiméntis albis, et in capítibus eórum corónæ áureæ.
content.english: 4 And round about the throne were four and twenty seats; and upon the seats, four and twenty ancients sitting, clothed in white garments, and on their heads were crowns of gold.

segments.t: Et in circúitu sedis sedília vigínti quátuor: et super thronos vigínti quátuor senióres sedéntes, circumamícti vestiméntis albis, et in capítibus eórum corónæ áureæ.

content.latin: 5 Et de throno procedébant fúlgura, et voces, et tonítrua: et septem lámpades ardéntes ante thronum, qui sunt septem spíritus Dei.
content.english: 5 And from the throne proceeded lightnings, and voices, and thunders; and there were seven lamps burning before the throne, which are the seven spirits of God.

segments.t: Et de throno procedébant fúlgura, et voces, et tonítrua: et septem lámpades ardéntes ante thronum, qui sunt septem spíritus Dei.

content.latin: 6 Et in conspéctu sedis tamquam mare vítreum símile crystállo: et in médio sedis, et in circúitu sedis quátuor animália plena óculis ante et retro.
content.english: 6 And in the sight of the throne was, as it were, a sea of glass like to crystal; and in the midst of the throne, and round about the throne, were four living creatures, full of eyes before and behind.

segments.t: Et in conspéctu sedis tamquam mare vítreum símile crystállo: et in médio sedis, et in circúitu sedis quátuor animália plena óculis ante et retro.

content.latin: 7 Et ánimal primum símile leóni, et secúndum ánimal símile vítulo, et tértium ánimal habens fáciem quasi hóminis, et quartum ánimal símile áquilæ volánti.
content.english: 7 And the first living creature was like a lion: and the second living creature like a calf: and the third living creature, having the face, as it were, of a man: and the fourth living creature was like an eagle flying.

segments.t: Et ánimal primum símile leóni, et secúndum ánimal símile vítulo, et tértium ánimal habens fáciem quasi hóminis, et quartum ánimal símile áquilæ volánti.

content.latin: 8 Et quátuor animália, síngula eórum habébant alas senas: et in circúitu, et intus plena sunt óculis: et réquiem non habébant die ac nocte, dicéntia: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dóminus Deus omnípotens, qui erat, et qui est, et qui ventúrus est.
content.english: 8 And the four living creatures had each of them six wings; and round about and within they are full of eyes. And they rested not day and night, saying: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, who was, and who is, and who is to come.

segments.t: Et quátuor animália, síngula eórum habébant alas senas: et in circúitu, et intus plena sunt óculis: et réquiem non habébant die ac nocte, dicéntia: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dóminus Deus omnípotens, qui erat, et qui est, et qui ventúrus est.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Vidi Dóminum sedéntem super sólium excélsum et elevátum, et plena erat omnis terra maiestáte eius:
content.english: ℟. I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and the whole earth was full of His glory;

segments.t: Vidi Dóminum sedéntem super sólium excélsum et elevátum, et plena erat omnis terra maiestáte eius:

content.latin: * Et ea, quæ sub ipso erant, replébant templum.
content.english: * And His train filled the temple.

content.latin: ℣. Séraphim stabant super illud: sex alæ uni, et sex alæ álteri.
content.english: ℣. Above it stood the Seraphim each one had six wings.

segments.t: Séraphim stabant super illud: sex alæ uni, et sex alæ álteri.

content.latin: ℟. Et ea, quæ sub ipso erant, replébant templum.
content.english: ℟. And His train filled the temple.

segments.t: Et ea, quæ sub ipso erant, replébant templum.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 1 Et vidi in déxtera sedéntis supra thronum, librum scriptum intus et foris, signátum sigíllis septem.
content.english: 1 And I saw in the right hand of him that sat on the throne, a book written within and without, sealed with seven seals.

segments.t: Et vidi in déxtera sedéntis supra thronum, librum scriptum intus et foris, signátum sigíllis septem.

content.latin: 2 Et vidi ángelum fortem, prædicántem voce magna: Quis est dignus aperíre librum, et sólvere signácula eius?
content.english: 2 And I saw a strong angel, proclaiming with a loud voice: Who is worthy to open the book, and to loose the seals thereof?

segments.t: Et vidi ángelum fortem, prædicántem voce magna: Quis est dignus aperíre librum, et sólvere signácula eius?

content.latin: 3 Et nemo póterat neque in cælo, neque in terra, neque subtus terram aperíre librum, neque respícere illum.
content.english: 3 And no man was able, neither in heaven, nor on earth, nor under the earth, to open the book, nor to look on it.

segments.t: Et nemo póterat neque in cælo, neque in terra, neque subtus terram aperíre librum, neque respícere illum.

content.latin: 4 Et ego flebam multum, quóniam nemo dignus invéntus est aperíre librum, nec vidére eum.
content.english: 4 And I wept much, because no man was found worthy to open the book, nor to see it.

segments.t: Et ego flebam multum, quóniam nemo dignus invéntus est aperíre librum, nec vidére eum.

content.latin: 5 Et unus de senióribus dixit mihi: Ne fléveris: ecce vicit leo de tribu Iuda, radix David, aperíre librum, et sólvere septem signácula eius.
content.english: 5 And one of the ancients said to me: Weep not; behold the lion of the tribe of Juda, the root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.

segments.t: Et unus de senióribus dixit mihi: Ne fléveris: ecce vicit leo de tribu Iuda, radix David, aperíre librum, et sólvere septem signácula eius.

content.latin: 6 Et vidi: et ecce in médio throni et quátuor animálium, et in médio seniórum, Agnum stantem tamquam occísum, habéntem córnua septem, et óculos septem: qui sunt septem spíritus Dei, missi in omnem terram.
content.english: 6 And I saw: and behold in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the midst of the ancients, a Lamb standing as it were slain, having seven horns and seven eyes: which are the seven Spirits of God, sent forth into all the earth.

segments.t: Et vidi: et ecce in médio throni et quátuor animálium, et in médio seniórum, Agnum stantem tamquam occísum, habéntem córnua septem, et óculos septem: qui sunt septem spíritus Dei, missi in omnem terram.

content.latin: 7 Et venit: et accépit de déxtera sedéntis in throno librum.
content.english: 7 And he came and took the book out of the right hand of him that sat on the throne.

segments.t: Et venit: et accépit de déxtera sedéntis in throno librum.

content.latin: 8 Et cum aperuísset librum, quátuor animália, et vigínti quátuor senióres cecidérunt coram Agno, habéntes sínguli cítharas, et phíalas áureas plenas odoramentórum, quæ sunt oratiónes sanctórum:
content.english: 8 And when he had opened the book, the four living creatures, and the four and twenty ancients fell down before the Lamb, having every one of them harps, and golden vials full of odours, which are the prayers of saints:

segments.t: Et cum aperuísset librum, quátuor animália, et vigínti quátuor senióres cecidérunt coram Agno, habéntes sínguli cítharas, et phíalas áureas plenas odoramentórum, quæ sunt oratiónes sanctórum:

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Beáta es Virgo María, Dei Génetrix, quæ credidísti Dómino: perfécta sunt in te quæ dicta sunt tibi: ecce exaltáta es super choros Angelórum:
content.english: ℟. O Virgin Mary, Mother of God, blessed art thou that didst believe the Lord, for there hath been a performance of those things which were told thee from the Lord. Behold, thou art exalted over choirs of Angels.

segments.t: Beáta es Virgo María, Dei Génetrix, quæ credidísti Dómino: perfécta sunt in te quæ dicta sunt tibi: ecce exaltáta es super choros Angelórum:

content.latin: * Intercéde pro nobis ad Dóminum, Deum nostrum.
content.english: * Plead for us with the Lord our God.

content.latin: ℣. Ave, María, grátia plena, Dóminus tecum.
content.english: ℣. Hail, Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee.

segments.t: Ave, María, grátia plena, Dóminus tecum.

content.latin: ℟. Intercéde pro nobis ad Dóminum, Deum nostrum.
content.english: ℟. Plead for us with the Lord our God.

segments.t: Intercéde pro nobis ad Dóminum, Deum nostrum.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 9 Et cantábant cánticum novum, dicéntes: Dignus es, Dómine, accípere librum, et aperíre signácula eius: quóniam occísus es, et redemísti nos Deo in sánguine tuo ex omni tribu, et lingua, et pópulo, et natióne:
content.english: 9 And they sung a new canticle, saying: Thou art worthy, O Lord, to take the book, and to open the seals thereof; because thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God, in thy blood, out of every tribe, and tongue, and people, and nation.

segments.t: Et cantábant cánticum novum, dicéntes: Dignus es, Dómine, accípere librum, et aperíre signácula eius: quóniam occísus es, et redemísti nos Deo in sánguine tuo ex omni tribu, et lingua, et pópulo, et natióne:

content.latin: 10 Et fecísti nos Deo nostro regnum, et sacerdótes: et regnábimus super terram.
content.english: 10 And hast made us to our God a kingdom and priests, and we shall reign on the earth.

segments.t: Et fecísti nos Deo nostro regnum, et sacerdótes: et regnábimus super terram.

content.latin: 11 Et vidi, et audívi vocem angelórum multórum in circúitu throni, et animálium, et seniórum: et erat númerus eórum míllia míllium,
content.english: 11 And I beheld, and I heard the voice of many angels round about the throne, and the living creatures, and the ancients; and the number of them was thousands of thousands,

segments.t: Et vidi, et audívi vocem angelórum multórum in circúitu throni, et animálium, et seniórum: et erat númerus eórum míllia míllium,

content.latin: 12 Dicéntium voce magna: Dignus est Agnus, qui occísus est, accípere virtútem, et divinitátem, et sapiéntiam, et fortitúdinem, et honórem, et glóriam, et benedictiónem.
content.english: 12 Saying with a loud voice: The Lamb that was slain is worthy to receive power, and divinity, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and benediction.

segments.t: Dicéntium voce magna: Dignus est Agnus, qui occísus est, accípere virtútem, et divinitátem, et sapiéntiam, et fortitúdinem, et honórem, et glóriam, et benedictiónem.

content.latin: 13 Et omnem creatúram, quæ in cælo est, et super terram, et sub terra, et quæ sunt in mari, et quæ in eo: omnes audívi dicéntes: Sedénti in throno, et Agno, benedíctio et honor, et glória, et potéstas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: 13 And every creature, which is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and such as are in the sea, and all that are in them: I heard all saying: To him that sitteth on the throne, and to the Lamb, benediction, and honour, and glory, and power, for ever and ever.

segments.t: Et omnem creatúram, quæ in cælo est, et super terram, et sub terra, et quæ sunt in mari, et quæ in eo: omnes audívi dicéntes: Sedénti in throno, et Agno, benedíctio et honor, et glória, et potéstas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: 14 Et quátuor animália dicébant: Amen. Et vigínti quátuor senióres cecidérunt in fácies suas: et adoravérunt vivéntem in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: 14 And the four living creatures said: Amen. And the four and twenty ancients fell down on their faces, and adored him that liveth for ever and ever.

segments.t: Et quátuor animália dicébant: Amen. Et vigínti quátuor senióres cecidérunt in fácies suas: et adoravérunt vivéntem in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. In conspéctu Angelórum psallam tibi:
content.english: ℟. Before the Angels will I sing praise unto thee, and will worship toward thy holy temple.

segments.t: In conspéctu Angelórum psallam tibi:

content.latin: * Et adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum, et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine.
content.english: * And I will praise thy Name, O Lord.

content.latin: ℣. Super misericórdia tua et veritáte tua, quóniam magnificásti super nos nomen sanctum tuum.
content.english: ℣. For thy lovingkindness and for thy truth; for Thou hast glorified thine holy Name on us.

segments.t: Super misericórdia tua et veritáte tua, quóniam magnificásti super nos nomen sanctum tuum.

content.latin: ℟. Et adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum, et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine.
content.english: ℟. And I will praise thy Name, O Lord.

segments.t: Et adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum, et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Et adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum, et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine.
content.english: ℟. And I will praise thy Name, O Lord.

segments.t: Et adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum, et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine.

content.latin: Nocturnus II
content.english: Nocturn II

segments.t: Nocturnus II

content.latin: Ant. Dómine, * qui operáti sunt iustítiam, habitábunt in tabernáculo tuo, et requiéscent in monte sancto tuo.
content.english: Ant. They that work righteousness, * O Lord, even they, shall abide in thy tabernacle, and dwell in thy holy Hill.

segments.t: Ant.
Dómine, * qui operáti sunt iustítiam, habitábunt in tabernáculo tuo, et requiéscent in monte sancto tuo.

content.latin: Psalmus 14 [4]
content.english: Psalm 14 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 14

content.latin: 14:1 Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo? * aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo?
content.english: 14:1 Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? * or who shall rest in thy holy hill?

segments.t: Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo? * aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo?

content.latin: 14:2 Qui ingréditur sine mácula, * et operátur iustítiam:
content.english: 14:2 He that walketh without blemish, * and worketh justice:

segments.t: Qui ingréditur sine mácula, * et operátur iustítiam:

content.latin: 14:3 Qui lóquitur veritátem in corde suo, * qui non egit dolum in lingua sua:
content.english: 14:3 He that speaketh truth in his heart, * who hath not used deceit in his tongue:

segments.t: Qui lóquitur veritátem in corde suo, * qui non egit dolum in lingua sua:

content.latin: 14:3 Nec fecit próximo suo malum, * et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos.
content.english: 14:3 Nor hath done evil to his neighbour: * nor taken up a reproach against his neighbours.

segments.t: Nec fecit próximo suo malum, * et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos.

content.latin: 14:4 Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu eius malígnus: * timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat:
content.english: 14:4 In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing: * but he glorifieth them that fear the Lord:

segments.t: Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu eius malígnus: * timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat:

content.latin: 14:4 Qui iurat próximo suo, et non décipit, * qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram, et múnera super innocéntem non accépit.
content.english: 14:4 He that sweareth to his neighbour, and deceiveth not; * He that hath not put out his money to usury, nor taken bribes against the innocent:

segments.t: Qui iurat próximo suo, et non décipit, * qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram, et múnera super innocéntem non accépit.

content.latin: 14:5 Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum.
content.english: 14:5 He that doth these things, * shall not be moved for ever.

segments.t: Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Dómine, qui operáti sunt iustítiam, habitábunt in tabernáculo tuo, et requiéscent in monte sancto tuo.
content.english: Ant. They that work righteousness, O Lord, even they, shall abide in thy tabernacle, and dwell in thy holy Hill.

segments.t: Ant.
Dómine, qui operáti sunt iustítiam, habitábunt in tabernáculo tuo, et requiéscent in monte sancto tuo.

content.latin: Ant. Hæc est generátio * quæréntium Dóminum, quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.
content.english: Ant. This is the generation of them that seek the Lord, * that seek the face of the God of Jacob.

segments.t: Ant.
Hæc est generátio * quæréntium Dóminum, quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.

content.latin: Psalmus 23 [5]
content.english: Psalm 23 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 23

content.latin: 23:1 Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo eius: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.
content.english: 23:1 The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof: * the world, and all they that dwell therein.

segments.t: Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo eius: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.

content.latin: 23:2 Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.
content.english: 23:2 For he hath founded it upon the seas; * and hath prepared it upon the rivers.

segments.t: Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.

content.latin: 23:3 Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto eius?

content.english: 31:2 Blessed is the man to whom the Lord hath not imputed sin, * and in whose spirit there is no guile.

segments.t: Quóniam tácui, inveteravérunt ossa mea, * dum clamárem tota die.

content.latin: 31:4 Quóniam die ac nocte graváta est super me manus tua: * convérsus sum in ærúmna mea, dum confígitur spina.
content.english: 31:4 For day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: * I am turned in my anguish, whilst the thorn is fastened.

segments.t: Quóniam die ac nocte graváta est super me manus tua: * convérsus sum in ærúmna mea, dum confígitur spina.

content.latin: 31:5 Delíctum meum cógnitum tibi feci: * et iniustítiam meam non abscóndi.
content.english: 31:5 I have acknowledged my sin to thee, * and my injustice I have not concealed.

segments.t: Verúmtamen in dilúvio aquárum multárum, * ad eum non approximábunt.

content.english: 31:7 Thou art my refuge from the trouble which hath encompassed me: * my joy, deliver me from them that surround me.

segments.t: Tu es refúgium meum a tribulatióne, quæ circúmdedit me: * exsultátio mea, érue me a circumdántibus me.

content.english: 31:8 I will give thee understanding, and I will instruct thee in this way, in which thou shalt go: * I will fix my eyes upon thee.

segments.t: Intelléctum tibi dabo, et ínstruam te in via hac, qua gradiéris: * firmábo super te óculos meos.

segments.t: Nolíte fíeri sicut equus et mulus, * quibus non est intelléctus.

content.english: 31:10 Many are the scourges of the sinner, * but mercy shall encompass him that hopeth in the Lord.

content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Sermo sancti Bedæ Venerábilis Presbýteri
content.english: From the Sermons of the Venerable Bede, Priest at Jarrow.

content.latin: Sermo 18 de Sanctis
content.english: 18th upon the Saints

segments.t: Sermo 18 de Sanctis

content.latin: Hódie, dilectíssimi, ómnium Sanctórum sub una solemnitátis lætítia celebrámus festivitátem: quorum societáte cælum exsúltat, quorum patrocíniis terra lætátur, triúmphis Ecclésia sancta coronátur, quorum conféssio quanto in passióne fórtior, tanto est clárior in honóre: quia, dum crevit pugna, crevit et pugnántium glória, et martýrii triúmphus multíplici passiónum génere adornátur: perque gravióra torménta, gravióra fuére et prǽmia: dum cathólica mater Ecclésia, quæ per totum orbem longe latéque diffúsa est, in ipso cápite suo Christo Iesu edúcta est, contumélias, cruces et mortem non timére; magis magísque roboráta, non resisténdo, sed perferéndo, univérsis, quos ágmine ínclito carcer pœnális inclúsit, pari et símili calóre virtútis ad geréndum certámen, glóriam triumphálem inspirávit.
content.english: Dearly beloved brethren: This day we keep, with one great cry of joy, a Feast in memory of all God's holy children; His children, whose presence is a gladness to heaven; His children, whose prayers are a blessing to earth; His children, whose victories are the crown of the Holy Church; His chosen, whose testifying is the more glorious in honour, as the agony in which it was given was the sterner in intensity, for as the dreader grew the battle, so the grander grew the fighters, and the triumph of martyrdom waxed the more incisive by the multiplicity of suffering, and the heavier the torment the heavier the prize. And it is our Mother, the Catholic Church, spread far and wide throughout all this planet, it is she that hath learnt, in Christ Jesus her Head, not to fear shame, nor cross, nor death, but hath waxed lealer and lealer, and, not by fighting, but by enduring, hath breathed into all that noble band who have come up to the bitter starting-post the hope of conquest and glory which hath warmed them manfully to accept the race.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: O vere beáta mater Ecclésia, quam sic honor divínæ dignatiónis illúminat, quam vincéntium gloriósus Mártyrum sanguis exórnat, quam inviolátæ confessiónis cándida índuit virgínitas! Flóribus eius nec rosæ nec lília desunt. Certent nunc caríssimi, sínguli, ut ad utrósque honóres amplíssimam accípiant dignitátem, corónas, vel de virginitáte cándidas, vel de passióne purpúreas. In cæléstibus castris pax et ácies habent flores suos, quibus mílites Christi coronántur.
content.english: If a verity thou art blessed, O my Mother the Church! The blaze of God's mercy beateth full upon thee; thine adornment is the glorious blood of victorious Martyrs, and thy raiment the virgin whiteness of untarnished orthodoxy. thy garlands lack neither roses nor lilies. And now, dearly beloved brethren, let each one of us strive to gain the goodly crown of one sort or the other, either the glistening whiteness of purity, or the red dye of suffering. In the army in heaven peace and war have both chaplets of their own, to crown Christ's soldiers withal.

segments.t: O

vere beáta mater Ecclésia, quam sic honor divínæ dignatiónis illúminat, quam vincéntium gloriósus Mártyrum sanguis exórnat, quam inviolátæ confessiónis cándida índuit virgínitas! content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Dei enim ineffábilis et imménsa bónitas étiam hoc provídit, ut labórum quidem tempus et agónis non exténderet, nec longum fáceret, aut ætérnum, sed breve, et ut ita dicam, momentáneum: ut in hac brevi et exígua vita agónes essent et labóres; in illa vero quæ ætérna est, corónæ et prǽmia meritórum: ut labóres quidem cito finiréntur, meritórum vero prǽmia sine fine durárent: ut post huius mundi ténebras visúri essent candidíssimam lucem, et acceptúri maiórem passiónum cunctárum acerbitátibus beatitúdinem, testánte hoc idem Apóstolo, ubi ait: Non sunt condígnæ passiónes huius témporis ad superventúram glóriam, quæ revelábitur in nobis.
content.english: Moreover, to this also hath the unutterable and boundless goodness of God seen, that He spreadeth not the time of working and wrestling, neither maketh it long, nor everlasting, and, as it were, but for a moment, so that in this short and scanty life there is wrestling and working, but the crown and the prize is in a life which is eternal. So the work is soon over, but the wage is paid for ever. And when the night of this world is over, the Saints are to see the clearness of the essential light, and to receive a blessedness outweighing the pangs of any torment, as testifieth the Apostle Paul, where he saith: The sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us. Rom. viii. 18.

content.english: 33:3 In the Lord shall my soul be praised: * let the meek hear and rejoice.

segments.t: In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea: * áudiant mansuéti, et læténtur.

content.latin: 33:4 Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen eius in idípsum.
content.english: 33:4 O magnify the Lord with me; * and let us extol his name together.

segments.t: Magnificáte Dóminum mecum: * et exaltémus nomen eius in idípsum.

content.latin: 33:5 Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.
content.english: 33:5 I sought the Lord, and he heard me; * and he delivered me from all my troubles.

segments.t: Exquisívi Dóminum, et exaudívit me: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus meis erípuit me.

content.latin: 33:6 Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.
content.english: 33:6 Come ye to him and be enlightened: * and your faces shall not be confounded.

segments.t: Accédite ad eum, et illuminámini: * et fácies vestræ non confundéntur.

content.latin: 33:7 Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus eius salvávit eum.
content.english: 33:7 This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him: * and saved him out of all his troubles.

segments.t: Iste pauper clamávit, et Dóminus exaudívit eum: * et de ómnibus tribulatiónibus eius salvávit eum.

content.latin: 33:8 Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.
content.english: 33:8 The Angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him: * and shall deliver them.

segments.t: Immíttet Ángelus Dómini in circúitu timéntium eum: * et erípiet eos.

content.latin: 33:9 Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.
content.english: 33:9 O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet: * blessed is the man that hopeth in him.

segments.t: Gustáte, et vidéte quóniam suávis est Dóminus: * beátus vir, qui sperat in eo.

content.latin: 33:10 Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti eius: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.
content.english: 33:10 Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: * for there is no want to them that fear him.

segments.t: Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti eius: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.

content.latin: 33:11 Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.
content.english: 33:11 The rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger: * but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good.

segments.t: Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.

content.latin: 33:12 Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.
content.english: 33:12 Come, children, hearken to me: * I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

segments.t: Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.

content.latin: 33:13 Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?
content.english: 33:13 Who is the man that desireth life: * who loveth to see good days?

segments.t: Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?

content.latin: 33:14 Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.
content.english: 33:14 Keep thy tongue from evil, * and thy lips from speaking guile.

segments.t: Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.

content.latin: 33:15 Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.
content.english: 33:15 Turn away from evil and do good: * seek after peace and pursue it.

segments.t: Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.

content.latin: 33:16 Óculi Dómini super iustos: * et aures eius in preces eórum.
content.english: 33:16 The eyes of the Lord are upon the just: * and his ears unto their prayers.

segments.t: Óculi Dómini super iustos: * et aures eius in preces eórum.

content.latin: 33:17 Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.
content.english: 33:17 But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things: * to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.

segments.t: Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.

content.latin: 33:18 Clamavérunt iusti, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.
content.english: 33:18 The just cried, and the Lord heard them: * and delivered them out of all their troubles.

segments.t: Clamavérunt iusti, et Dóminus exaudívit eos: * et ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus eórum liberávit eos.

content.latin: 33:19 Iuxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.
content.english: 33:19 The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart: * and he will save the humble of spirit.

segments.t: Iuxta est Dóminus iis, qui tribuláto sunt corde: * et húmiles spíritu salvábit.

content.latin: 33:20 Multæ tribulatiónes iustórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.
content.english: 33:20 Many are the afflictions of the just; * but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.

segments.t: Multæ tribulatiónes iustórum: * et de ómnibus his liberábit eos Dóminus.

content.latin: 33:21 Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.
content.english: 33:21 The Lord keepeth all their bones, * not one of them shall be broken.

segments.t: Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.

content.latin: 33:22 Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt iustum, delínquent.
content.english: 33:22 The death of the wicked is very evil: * and they that hate the just shall be guilty.

segments.t: Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt iustum, delínquent.

content.latin: 33:23 Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.
content.english: 33:23 The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants: * and none of them that trust in him shall offend.

segments.t: Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Timéte Dóminum omnes Sancti eius, quóniam nihil deest timéntibus eum: ecce óculi Dómini super iustos, et aures eius ad preces eórum.
content.english: Ant. O fear the Lord, all ye His Saints, for there is no want to them that fear Him. Behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears are open unto their cry.

content.english: Ant. O Lord, Thou hast been a shelter for thy Saints, * a strong tower from the enemy. Thou hast given the heritage to those that fear thy Name, and they shall abide in thy tabernacle for ever.

content.english: Psalm 60 [8]

content.latin: 60:2 Exáudi, Deus, deprecatiónem meam: * inténde oratióni meæ.
content.english: 60:2 Hear, O God, my supplication: * be attentive to my prayer.

segments.t: Exáudi, Deus, deprecatiónem meam: * inténde oratióni meæ.

content.latin: 60:3 A fínibus terræ ad te clamávi: * dum anxiarétur cor meum, in petra exaltásti me.
content.english: 60:3 To thee have I cried from the ends of the earth: * when my heart was in anguish, thou hast exalted me on a rock.

segments.t: A fínibus terræ ad te clamávi: * dum anxiarétur cor meum, in petra exaltásti me.

content.latin: 60:4 Deduxísti me, quia factus es spes mea: * turris fortitúdinis a fácie inimíci.
content.english: 60:4 Thou hast conducted me; for thou hast been my hope: * a tower of strength against the face of the enemy.

segments.t: Deduxísti me, quia factus es spes mea: * turris fortitúdinis a fácie inimíci.

content.latin: 60:5 Inhabitábo in tabernáculo tuo in sǽcula: * prótegar in velaménto alárum tuárum.
content.english: 60:5 In thy tabernacle I shall dwell for ever: * I shall be protected under the covert of thy wings.

segments.t: Inhabitábo in tabernáculo tuo in sǽcula: * prótegar in velaménto alárum tuárum.

content.latin: 60:6 Quóniam tu, Deus meus, exaudísti oratiónem meam: * dedísti hereditátem timéntibus nomen tuum.
content.english: 60:6 For thou, my God, hast heard my prayer: * thou hast given an inheritance to them that fear thy name.

segments.t: Quóniam tu, Deus meus, exaudísti oratiónem meam: * dedísti hereditátem timéntibus nomen tuum.

content.latin: 60:7 Dies super dies regis adícies: * annos eius usque in diem generatiónis et generatiónis.
content.english: 60:7 Thou wilt add days to the days of the king: * his years even to generation and generation.

segments.t: Dies super dies regis adícies: * annos eius usque in diem generatiónis et generatiónis.

content.latin: 60:8 Pérmanet in ætérnum in conspéctu Dei: * misericórdiam et veritátem eius quis requíret?
content.english: 60:8 He abideth for ever in the sight of God: * his mercy and truth who shall search?

segments.t: Pérmanet in ætérnum in conspéctu Dei: * misericórdiam et veritátem eius quis requíret?

content.latin: 60:9 Sic psalmum dicam nómini tuo in sǽculum sǽculi: * ut reddam vota mea de die in diem.
content.english: 60:9 So will I sing a psalm to thy name for ever and ever: * that I may pay my vows from day to day.

segments.t: Sic psalmum dicam nómini tuo in sǽculum sǽculi: * ut reddam vota mea de die in diem.

content.english: Psalm 96 [9]

content.latin: 96:1 Dóminus regnávit, exsúltet terra: * læténtur ínsulæ multæ.
content.english: 96:1 The Lord hath reigned, let the earth rejoice: * let many islands be glad.

segments.t: Dóminus regnávit, exsúltet terra: * læténtur ínsulæ multæ.

content.latin: 96:2 Nubes, et calígo in circúitu eius: * iustítia, et iudícium corréctio sedis eius.
content.english: 96:2 Clouds and darkness are round about him: * justice and judgment are the establishment of his throne.

segments.t: Nubes, et calígo in circúitu eius: * iustítia, et iudícium corréctio sedis eius.

content.latin: 96:3 Ignis ante ipsum præcédet, * et inflammábit in circúitu inimícos eius.
content.english: 96:3 A fire shall go before him, * and shall burn his enemies round about.

segments.t: Ignis ante ipsum præcédet, * et inflammábit in circúitu inimícos eius.

content.latin: 96:4 Illuxérunt fúlgura eius orbi terræ: * vidit, et commóta est terra.
content.english: 96:4 His lightnings have shone forth to the world: * the earth saw and trembled.

segments.t: Illuxérunt fúlgura eius orbi terræ: * vidit, et commóta est terra.

content.latin: 96:5 Montes, sicut cera fluxérunt a fácie Dómini: * a fácie Dómini omnis terra.
content.english: 96:5 The mountains melted like wax, at the presence of the Lord: * at the presence of the Lord of all the earth.

segments.t: Montes, sicut cera fluxérunt a fácie Dómini: * a fácie Dómini omnis terra.

content.latin: 96:6 Annuntiavérunt cæli iustítiam eius: * et vidérunt omnes pópuli glóriam eius.
content.english: 96:6 The heavens declared his justice: * and all people saw his glory.

segments.t: Annuntiavérunt cæli iustítiam eius: * et vidérunt omnes pópuli glóriam eius.

content.latin: 96:7 Confundántur omnes, qui adórant sculptília: * et qui gloriántur in simulácris suis.
content.english: 96:7 Let them be all confounded that adore graven things, * and that glory in their idols.

segments.t: Confundántur omnes, qui adórant sculptília: * et qui gloriántur in simulácris suis.

content.english: 96:7 Adore him, all you his angels: * Sion heard, and was glad.

segments.t: Adoráte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * audívit, et lætáta est Sion.

content.english: 96:8 And the daughters of Juda rejoiced, * because of thy judgments, O Lord.

segments.t: Et exsultavérunt fíliæ Iudæ, * propter iudícia tua, Dómine:

content.english: 96:9 For thou art the most high Lord over all the earth: * thou art exalted exceedingly above all gods.

segments.t: Quóniam tu Dóminus Altíssimus super omnem terram: * nimis exaltátus es super omnes deos.

content.latin: 96:10 Qui dilígitis Dóminum, odíte malum: * custódit Dóminus ánimas sanctórum suórum, de manu peccatóris liberábit eos.
content.english: 96:10 You that love the Lord, hate evil: * the Lord preserveth the souls of his saints, he will deliver them out of the hand of the sinner.

segments.t: Qui dilígitis Dóminum, odíte malum: * custódit Dóminus ánimas sanctórum suórum, de manu peccatóris liberábit eos.

content.latin: 96:11 Lux orta est iusto, * et rectis corde lætítia.
content.english: 96:11 Light is risen to the just, * and joy to the right of heart.

segments.t: Lux orta est iusto, * et rectis corde lætítia.

content.english: 96:12 Rejoice, ye just, in the Lord: * and give praise to the remembrance of his holiness.

content.english: ℟. Their reward also is with the Lord.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.english: Homily by St. Augustine, Bishop of Hippo.

content.latin: Lib. 1 de Sermone Domini in monte, sub initium
content.english: Bk. I on the Lord's Sermon

segments.t: Lib. 1 de Sermone Domini in monte, sub initium

content.latin: Si quǽritur quid signíficet mons, bene intellégitur significáre maióra præcépta iustítiæ, quia minóra erant quæ Iudǽis data sunt. Unus tamen Deus per sanctos prophétas et fámulos suos, secúndum ordinatíssimam distributiónem témporum, dedit minóra præcépta pópulo, quem adhuc timóre alligári oportébat: et per Fílium suum maióra pópulo, quem caritáte iam liberári convénerat. Cum autem minóra minóribus, maióra maióribus dantur, ab eo dantur, qui solus novit congruéntem suis tempóribus géneri humáno exhibére medicínam.
content.english: If it be asked what is signified by the mountain, the said mountain may well be understood to figure the higher and greater commandments of righteousness, since those that have been given to the Jews are the lesser. The one God, in an excellent order of times, gave, by His holy Prophets and servants, His lesser commandments unto the people whom it still behoved to be bound by fear, but by His Son He gave the greater unto the people whom it now beseemed to set free by love. But whether it be the lesser to the lesser, or the greater to the greater, all are alike the gift of Him Who alone knoweth what is in each epoch the seasonable medicine of mankind.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Sint lumbi vestri præcíncti, et lucérnæ ardéntes in mánibus vestris:
content.english: ℟. Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning;

segments.t: Sint lumbi vestri præcíncti, et lucérnæ ardéntes in mánibus vestris:

content.latin: * Et vos símiles homínibus exspectántibus dóminum suum, quando revertátur a núptiis.
content.english: * And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.

content.english: ℣. Watch therefore, for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.

content.latin: Nec mirum est, quod dantur præcépta maióra propter regnum cælórum, et minóra data sunt propter regnum terrénum, ab eódem uno Deo, qui fecit cælum et terram. De hac ergo iustítia, quæ maior est, per prophétam dícitur: Iustítia tua sicut montes Dei: et hoc bene signíficat, quod ab uno magístro, solo docéndis tantis rebus idóneo, docétur in monte. Sedens autem docet, quod pértinet ad dignitátem magistérii. Et accédunt ad eum discípuli eius, ut audiéndis illíus verbis hi essent étiam córpore vicinióres, qui præcéptis adimpléndis étiam ánimo propinquábant. Et apériens os suum docébat eos, dicens. Ista circumlocútio, qua scríbitur, Et apériens os suum, fortássis ipsa mora comméndat aliquánto longiórem futúrum esse sermónem. Nisi forte non vacet, quod nunc eum dictum est aperuísse os suum, quod ipse in lege véteri aperíre soléret ora prophetárum.
content.english: Neither is it marvel that the greater commandments be given touching the kingdom of heaven, and the lesser touching a commonwealth upon earth, since both are alike the gifts of that one God Who is the Maker alike of heaven and of earth. The higher and greater righteousness, then, is that whereof the Prophet saith: Thy righteousness is like the mountains of God. Ps. xxxv. 7. Thus is that Teacher, Who alone can give such teaching, mystically represented as teaching upon a mountain. And when He was set. The attitude of sitting while teaching appertaineth to the majesty of His instruction. His disciples came unto Him nearer in the body, to hear those precepts, by the fulfillment of which they should be nearer in spirit. And He opened His Mouth, and taught them, saying these words appear redundant to the sense. It may possibly be that this more pompous introduction is adopted on account of the exceptional length of the discourse to follow. But it may also be that these words are not really redundant, but the pointed declaration that He now opened His Own Mouth, Who, under the Old Law, had been used to open the mouths of the Prophets.

content.latin: Quid ergo dicit? Beáti páuperes spíritu: quóniam ipsórum est regnum cælórum. Légimus scriptum de appetitióne rerum temporálium: Omnia vánitas, et præsúmptio spíritus. Præsúmptio autem spíritus, audáciam et supérbiam signíficat. Vulgo étiam magnos spíritus supérbi habére dicúntur: et recte, quandóquidem spíritus étiam ventus vocátur. Unde scriptum est: Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum. Quis vero nésciat supérbos inflátos dici, tamquam vento disténtos? Unde est étiam illud Apóstoli: Sciéntia inflat, cáritas vero ædíficat. Quaprópter recte hic intellegúntur páuperes spíritu, húmiles et timéntes Deum, id est, non habéntes inflántem spíritum.
content.english: And now, what saith He? Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. We have read where it is written concerning the lusting after temporal things: The wandering of the desire is vanity and presumption of spirit. Eccl. vi. 9. Presumption of spirit signifieth rashness and pride. We are used to say of proud people that they are men of high spirit, and we say well, since spirit is only one of the Latin names for wind. It is so used, for instance, in Ps. cxlviii. 8, Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy wind. Who hath not heard the proud spoken of as puffed up, as if they were blown out with wind? Hence, alas, the Apostle saith: Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth. 1 Cor. viii. 1. By the poor in spirit, who are here called blessed, are rightly to be understood such as are lowly and fear God, that is, have not got minds puffed up with windy vanity.

content.latin: 62:6 Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.
content.english: 62:6 Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: * and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.

segments.t: Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.

content.latin: 62:7 Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.
content.english: 62:7 If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning: * because thou hast been my helper.

segments.t: Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.

content.latin: 62:8 Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.
content.english: 62:8 And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings: my soul hath stuck close to thee: * thy right hand hath received me.

segments.t: Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.

content.latin: 62:10 Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.
content.english: 62:10 But they have sought my soul in vain, they shall go into the lower parts of the earth: * they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.

segments.t: Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.

content.latin: 62:12 Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.
content.english: 62:12 But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: * because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.

segments.t: Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Redemísti nos, Dómine Deus, in sánguine tuo ex omni tribu, et lingua, et pópulo, et natióne, et fecísti nos Deo nostro regnum.
content.english: Ant. Thou, O Lord God, hast redeemed us by thy Blood, out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation, and hast made us a kingdom unto our God.

segments.t: Ant.
Redemísti nos, Dómine Deus, in sánguine tuo ex omni tribu, et lingua, et pópulo, et natióne, et fecísti nos Deo nostro regnum.

segments.t: Ant.
Benedícite Dóminum * omnes elécti eius: ágite dies lætítiæ, et confitémini illi.

content.latin: 3:57 Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:57 All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:58 Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:58 O ye angels of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye heavens, bless the Lord:

segments.t: Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:59 Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:59 O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord: * O all ye powers of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:60 Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:60 O ye sun and moon, bless the Lord: * O ye stars of heaven, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:61 Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.
content.english: 3:61 O every shower and dew, bless ye the Lord: * O all ye spirits of God, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:62 Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:62 O ye fire and heat, bless the Lord: * O ye cold and heat, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:63 Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:63 O ye dews and hoar frosts, bless the Lord: * O ye frost and cold, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:64 Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.
content.english: 3:64 O ye ice and snow, bless the Lord: * O ye nights and days, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:65 Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.
content.english: 3:65 O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:66 Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:66 O let the earth bless the Lord: * let it praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:67 Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.
content.english: 3:67 O ye mountains and hills, bless the Lord: * O all ye things that spring up in the earth, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:68 Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.
content.english: 3:68 O ye fountains, bless the Lord: * O ye seas and rivers, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:69 Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:69 O ye whales, and all that move in the waters, bless the Lord: * O all ye fowls of the air, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:70 Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.
content.english: 3:70 O all ye beasts and cattle, bless the Lord: * O ye sons of men, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:71 Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:71 O let Israel bless the Lord: * let them praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:72 Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:72 O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:73 Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.
content.english: 3:73 O ye spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord: * O ye holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:74 Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:74 O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless ye the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:) Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:75 (Bow head) Let us bless the Father and the Son, with the Holy Ghost; * let us praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:)
Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:56 Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:56 Blessed art thou, O Lord, in the firmament of heaven: * and worthy of praise, and glorious for ever.

segments.t: Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.

content.latin: Psalmus 148 [5]
content.english: Psalm 148 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 148

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

segments.t: Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

segments.t: Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.

content.latin: 148:8 Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:
content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

segments.t: Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

segments.t: Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.

content.latin: 148:10 Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
content.english: 148:10 Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

segments.t: Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:

content.latin: 148:11 Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.
content.english: 148:11 Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

segments.t: Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.

content.latin: 148:12 Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.
content.english: 148:12 Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * For his name alone is exalted.

segments.t: Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.

content.latin: 148:14 Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.
content.english: 148:14 The praise of him is above heaven and earth: * and he hath exalted the horn of his people.

segments.t: Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.

content.latin: 148:14 Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.
content.english: 148:14 A hymn to all his saints: to the children of Israel, a people approaching him.

segments.t: Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Hymnus ómnibus Sanctis eius: fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi: glória hæc est ómnibus sanctis eius.
